tagline: Out of the old town center, north to Griswold.
intro: Route 164 leaves Preston City at its junction with Route 165 and goes north as Jewett City Road to the Griswold town line, a short scenic run. The direct way from the village to Jewett City became Route 164 in the 1932 renumbering, and its line has seen no major change since.

Preston City was set out in 1686 as the center of a farming town that fed the port of Norwich. Its good years ran from the Revolution to about 1830, when Preston farm goods went down the Thames and out to other east coast ports, and the farmers' and merchants' houses still show it.

moments.title: Preston City Baptist Church
moments.text: Built in 1812, the church was later turned to face a different way, and its three-stage steeple went up twenty years after the rest of it.

moments.title: Old Town Pound
moments.text: On Amos Road a stone-walled enclosure served the village as a pound, the kind of pen where British medieval villages held stray livestock.
